tools.name: find_operations
tools.description:
Find the operations that return the data you need, from what you would ask in words ("reviews of a
        restaurant on google maps", "places near a point"): the few that fit best, each with its id
        (source/resource/verb), when to use it, its options in one line (* is required), its record f

tools.name: get_operation
tools.description:
Everything about one operation, by its id from find_operations ("google_maps/reviews/list"): when to use
        it, its options with their defaults, every field of its records, its price, its errors, its changelog.

tools.name: run_operation
tools.description:
Run one operation (POST /v2/run) and get one page of records in `results`, with `count`, `cost` and
        `balance`. `options` is the operation's input (see find_operations or get_operation).

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description:
Tell lobstr.io's team what went wrong or what you need, from this session (POST /v2/feedback): an
        operation that failed in a way its error does not explain, a record that lacks a field you needed, an
        operation that does not exist yet, an error message that misled you. Free, never bil

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description:
The credits this connection's key can spend now, and the account's plan with what one credit costs on it
        (`plan.credit_price`; null on the free plan, whose credits have no price). To say a cost in money, multiply
        the credits by it; never guess a price.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "run_operation" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_operation, run_operation, send_feedback · Private data: find_operations, get_operation, run_operation, send_feedback · Public sink: run_operation, send_feedback · Destructive: find_operations, run_operation.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_operation, run_operation, send_feedback · Private data: find_operations, get_operation, run_operation, send_feedback · Public sink: run_operation, send_feedback · Destructive: find_operations, run_operation

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
